objections.claim: The guard as specified ("IF any line other than the affirmation line matches FINDING_BULLET_RE") skips the affirmation line entirely, but `matchAffirmation` accepts an affirmation sentence *followed by whitespace and a remainder on the same line* (`review-call.mjs` :743-745), and the existing same-line guards (`MID_LINE_SEVERITY_RE` / `MID_LINE_NAMESPACE_RE`) check only severity and namespace tokens — not bullets. So `No QA objection. - claim: the token is logged` on one line has its bullet-bearing remainder read by neither the new guard nor the MID_LINE guards, and the body normalises to clean — the exact silent-drop this ticket exists to close, reopened by a one-line variant of the input.
objections.evidence: Spec §"Triple-bullet guard in `normaliseCleanRefutation`" pseudocode ("any line other than the affirmation line"); `normaliser-excerpt.md` :740-748 (remainder is captured, not rejected) and :802-804 (MID_LINE guards cover severity/namespace only). The spec's own design principle "Never fail open on a finding" is violated on this path.
objections.predicted_consequence: A refuter that appends a finding bullet to its sign-off line is normalised to `### observation: no findings`, the lens reads `clear`, and the objection vanishes with no fault anywhere — the FAFF-1223 DONE item "a body with `### observation: no findings` plus a finding-shaped section returns `ok: false`" is defeated for the same-line form.

objections.claim: the normaliser guard is specified as "IF any line other than the affirmation line matches FINDING_BULLET_RE", and the prose says the check "covers lines before and after the affirmation" — but `matchAffirmation` explicitly permits a remainder after the sentence on the SAME line (`line.startsWith(entry.sentence)` + whitespace). A body like `No infosec objection. - claim: the token is logged` has its only triple bullet on the affirmation line, so the new guard never sees it, the body still normalises to `### observation: no findings`, and the finding is silently dropped — the exact failure this ticket exists to close, and a direct contradiction of the spec's own design principle "Never fail open on a finding."
objections.evidence: the "Triple-bullet guard in `normaliseCleanRefutation`" pseudocode and bullet list (HOW); the design principle "Never fail open on a finding" (Design principles); `matchAffirmation`'s remainder behaviour (review-call.mjs :740-748).
